1  Date : 17/07/2023  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal has been filed by the appellants - original claimants against the respondents - original opponents under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4062/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined referred to as 'the Act' for short)
against the judgment and award passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.), Fast Track Court No. 5, Ahmedabad (Rural) in MACP No. 891 of 1993 on 05.02.2007.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.), Fast Track Court No. 5, Ahmedabad (Rural
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The parties are hereinafter referred to as the claimants and the opponents as they stood in the original petition for the sake of convenience, clarity and brevity.

2. The brief facts that emerge from the record of the case are as under:
2.1.

That on 24.02.1993 at around 7.00pm, one Ranchhodbhai Patel was going in his loading rickshaw bearing registration No. GJ-1T-5343 on Ahmedabad - Kathlal Highway road and between village Bhavda and Kathiyana Muvada, the opponent No.1 came driving matador - 407 bearing registration No. GJ- 1U-4003, which was insured with the opponent No. 2 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed with the rickshaw, as a result of which, Ranchhodbhai Patel sustained serious injuries and succumbed to his injuries during the treatment.
The offence was registered at Kanbha Police Station being I- C.R.No.21 of 1993.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4062/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined 2.2

The claimants, who are the widow and son of deceased Ranchhodbhai, have filed the claim petition mainly stating that they have lost their sole earning member and deceased Ranchhodbhai was driving the rickshaw and earning Rs.3,000/- per month and was also earning Rs.12,000/- per annum by doing agricultural activities.

Hence, the claimants have claimed an amount of Rs.
7,50,000/- as compensation from the opponents jointly and severally under all the available heads.

3. The notices were served to the opponents and the opponent No.1 appeared through his advocate but did not file any written statement, whereas, the opponent No. 2 - insurance company appeared through its advocate and filed the written statement at Exh.19.

The opponent No. 2 - insurance company has mainly denied all the allegations made in the claim petition and has stated that the deceased himself was negligent for occurrence of the accident, and hence, the claim petition may be dismissed.
4. The learned Tribunal, after considering the oral as well as documentary evidence submitted by all the parties on record, held the opponent No.1 - driver of the matador to be 100% NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4062/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined negligent for occurrence of the accident and considering the monthly income of the deceased to be Rs.2,500/- per month,
added Rs.500/- as prospective income and after deducting 1/3 amount for personal expenditure,
applied the multiplier of 8, considering age of the deceased.

The learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,22,000/- including the amounts under the heads of loss of consortium, loss of estate, funeral Shardaben Ranchhodbhai Patel vs Mohamed Shafi Merumiya Chauhan on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119213337/
2 expenses and pain, shock and suffering to be recovered from the opponents jointly and severally with interest at the rate of 7.5% from the date of filing the claim petition till realization.
5. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award, the claimants have preferred the present appeal mainly stating that the award of the learned Tribunal is against the evidence on record and the learned Tribunal has not assessed the evidence that was led on record qua the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: That the learned Tribunal has not considered the prospective income and has applied the multiplier of 8, when, in fact, considering the age of the deceased, the multiplier of 11 should be applied, and hence, the claimants have claimed for enhancement of the amount of compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4062/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined
6. Heard learned advocate Mr. Kiran C. Mehta for the appellants and learned advocate Mr.G.C.Majmudar for the respondent No.2.
Though served, the respondent No. 1 has not appeared.

7. Learned advocate for the appellants has urged this Court to consider enhancement of the amount of compensation in light of the settled principles of law in the cases of Sarla Verma and others Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 1211 and National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 and has urged this Court to modify the amount of award accordingly.

sentences.text: 8. Learned advocate Mr.G.C.Majmudar for respondent No. 2 - has stated that the learned Tribunal has appreciated all the evidence properly and no order of interference in required, hence, the present appeal may be dismissed.
9. From the paper book of MACP No. 891 of 1993, it appears that the claimant No. 1 has deposed on oath at Exh. 41 and has narrated all the facts mentioned in the claim petition.

The claimant No. 1 has stated that deceased Ranchhodbhai had purchased the loading rickshaw bearing registration No.
GJ-1T- NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4062/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined 5343 from one Chinubhai Patel of Vahelal village.

That one middle man namely Ghanshyambhai had hired the rickshaw for bringing vegetables and fruits every morning from the village and accordingly,
deceased Ranchhodbhai was earning Rs.3000/- per month.

The claimants have also examined the said witness Ghanshyambhai at Exh. 44 and he has stated that he is doing the business of vegetables and collects the vegetables from the surroundings villages and sends them to the vegetable market at Jamalpur, Ahmedabad.
That deceased Ranchhodbhai was bringing the vegetables in his loading rickshaw and he was paying an amount of Rs.3,000/- per month to deceased Ranchhodbhai.

10. The claimants have produced copies of the FIR at Exh. 22, panchnam at Exh. 23, panchnama of the matador at Exh. 25, the inquest panchnama at Exh.27, post mortem report at Exh. 28 and on perusal of the documents, the factum of the accident is proved and

sentences.text: 3 Ghanshyambhai at Exh. 44, the claimants have proved that the deceased was earning an amount of Rs.3,000/- per month from his Rickshaw.

11. The learned Tribunal has observed these facts in the judgment NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4062/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined and award but has not believed the amount of income to be Rs.3,000/- as no documentary evidence was produced and has held the monthly income of the deceased to be Rs.2500/- per month.

This finding of the learned Tribunal appears to be erroneous as the claimants have proved from the deposition of witness Ghanshyambhai, the income of the deceased to be Rs.3000/- per month and hence, in light of the deposition of witness Ghanshyambhai, the learned Tribunal ought to have considered Rs.3000/- as monthly income of the deceased.
12.

Considering monthly income of the deceased to be Rs.3,000/-, from the P.M.Note at Exh.28, the age of deceased Ranchhodbhai is about 55 years and as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Supra), there should be no addition to the income of future prospects and hence, considering monthly income to be Rs.3000/- and deducing 1/3 amount

,
monthly loss of dependency would come to Rs.2000/ and accordingly, annual loss of dependency would be Rs.24,000/- and as the deceased is admittedly 55 years old, multiplier of 11 would be applied as per the ratio laid down in case of Sarla Varma (Supra) and the claimants would be entitled for an amount of Rs.2,64,000/- towards future loss of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4062/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined dependency.

As per the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the claimants are entitled to Rs.80,000/- towards loss of spousal and parental and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and in all, the claimants are entitled to Rs.3,74,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.2,20,000/- and hence, the claimants are entitled for enhanced amount of Rs.1,54,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

13. For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed and the judgment and award passed by the the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.), Fast Track Court No. 5, Ahmedabad (Rural) in MACP No. 891 of 1993 is hereby modified and in addition, the claimants are entitled to receive Rs.1,54,000/- as an additional amount with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced amount til realization.

The insurance company is directed to deposit the additional amount of compensation with 6% interest as early as possible within an outer limit of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4062/2008 JUDGMENT DATED:
17/07/2023 undefined copy of this order.
After depositing of the additional amount of compensation, the same shall be disbursed in favour of the claimants through NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification.
14. Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.
Pending civil application, if any, shall stand disposed of accordingly.
